stories.title: Trump says he will decide on resuming military action against Iran
stories.summary: President Trump said after meeting national security advisers that he will make a decision on resuming military action in the Iran war now that the U.S. midterm elections are over. Iran reportedly sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar, per Reuters. A senior Iranian official said it would be discussed only after the U.S. meets Iran's seven demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The outcome bears on regional security and on shipping through the strait.

stories.title: Wall Street rebounds after AI-led selloff; Nasdaq up 1.09% on Friday
stories.summary: On Nov. 6 the Nasdaq closed at 24,579.42 (+1.09%) and the S&P 500 at 7,376.86 (+0.31%), while the Dow fell 0.46% to 51,285.73. The rebound followed Thursday's AI-driven rout, when the Nasdaq Composite entered correction territory, with investors citing Democratic midterm wins by anti-AI candidates. October payrolls rose by 165,000 against 59,000 expected, and unemployment held at 4.1%. Oracle fell on a report that Microsoft was ending a computing contract with it.

stories.title: METR estimates Anthropic's AI progress is running at about twice its prior pace
stories.summary: The independent evaluator METR published an assessment on Nov. 5 based on a high-access evaluation at Anthropic from Aug. 12 to Oct. 29, 2026. Its best estimate is that Anthropic's capabilities on well-specified tasks are improving at about 2x its March 2024 to October 2025 rate, with an uncertainty range that includes 1.3x to 3x. METR attributes roughly 80% of the acceleration to AI and says compute scaling did not cause it. Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative, so the findings rely heavily on METR's judgment.

stories.title: NASA's Swift observatory re-enters Earth's atmosphere after nearly 22 years
stories.summary: NASA's Swift Observatory re-entered the atmosphere above North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7:39 a.m. EST, according to the U.S. Space Force. Launched in 2004 with a planned two-year mission, it operated for nearly 22 years. Swift studied gamma-ray bursts and rapidly turned its three telescopes toward sudden events to alert observatories worldwide. NASA expected most of the spacecraft to burn up, though some components might have survived.

stories.title: Paraguay's president resigns after major bank collapse
stories.summary: According to a New York Times report summarized by Just Security, Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned after a major bank with close ties to his administration collapsed. The collapse reportedly left about half of the population without access to their money. The lower house of Congress voted unanimously to proceed with impeachment.
stories.source: Just Security (citing The New York Times)

stories.title: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault in UK court
stories.summary: A U.K. court found Russell Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He will be sentenced on Monday, and the Metropolitan Police say two further rape investigations are ongoing.
